polityNote: The 10 counties (apskritys) of Lithuania as territorial units, from the abolition of the county governors’ administrations (1 Jul 2010) to the end of 2019; OpenHistoricalMap draws them as administrative units 1994–2010 (to 1 Jan 2011), and this dossier yields to it there. Atoms: geoBoundaries LTU ADM1 (OpenStreetMap/Wambacher 2017; ODbL), one atom per county; the 60 municipalities of the same publisher nest in them exactly (0 overlap, 0 hole at 0.02°). The outline dates from the municipal reform law of 21 Dec 1999 (Elektrėnai to Vilnius County, Pagėgiai to Tauragė County); no later change of a municipality is recorded. ① check: union areas against the Statistics Lithuania county areas (via Statoids) agree within −0.6%…−0.2% for 9 counties; Klaipėda −7.9%, the stated area including the Lithuanian part of the Curonian Lagoon.

sources.title: Vikipedija — Lietuvos apskritys
sources.says: The 1994 law (No. I-558) divided Lithuania into 10 counties; county governors’ administrations were abolished on 1 Jul 2010; the 10 counties remain as territorial, not administrative, units.

sources.title: Wikipedia — Counties of Lithuania
sources.says: Ten counties, divided into 60 municipalities; the division was created in 1994 and slightly modified in 2000; on 1 July 2010 the county administrations were abolished but the counties are retained.

sources.title: Vikipedija — Lietuvos administracinis suskirstymas
sources.says: Since the 1999–2000 municipal reform Lithuania has 60 municipalities; in 1995–2010 they were subordinate to 10 counties, abolished as administrative units but kept as territorial ones.

sources.title: Vikipedija — Savivaldybių reforma
sources.says: The reform law was adopted on 21 Dec 1999: new municipalities were split from large district municipalities and some municipal borders were moved.
